what: You walk a foggy (1→20) store aisle in first person. On both sides, every 2 units, stand chrome-rod clothes racks (two tiers × two bays, the clothing images always face the camera) and image·video panels, and three joined aisle sets loop so it runs endlessly. Wheel (Δ/50, every 60ms, stops after 0.5s of rest), W/S and ↑↓ add walking force, and speed follows by 1/20 of the remaining gap each frame, advancing at 0.1× scale. The head turns toward the cursor (left-right −2x clamped to ±1 then ×90°, up-down y×18°, 1/20 per frame). On open you drop from height 10 to eye level 1.6 by 1/20 per frame, and a wire shopping basket follows at .9 ahead. Hovering a shelf makes its clothes breathe at 1±.05 and come .2 forward with fx:hover, and pressing fires fx:pick. On video panels the pattern flows one panel per 10 seconds. Below panel width 768 you view the left shelf from the side (100° field of view), the prev·next buttons add a ±2.22 force (decaying by 1/10), and when you stop it settles by 1/10 onto the nearest bay (2)

options.layout: Aisle layout — two letters per row, left and right (P clothes rack · I image panel · V video panel), aisles separated by |. Default "PV PI PP VP PP PI PP | PP IP PP PV PP IP PP"
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Product — uses the img inside as the clothing picture, and shows a clothing silhouette placeholder if there is none. Rotated through the shelves in order (this order is the detail.index of fx:hover and fx:pick)
options.[data-fx-part=panel]: Slot name written on the image/video board (data-label) — cycled in turn
options.[data-fx-part=prev] · [data-fx-part=next: Button that moves one slot at a time on phone (hidden above 768)
options.fx:pause · fx:resume: Fired at an element, it stops walking and picking and hooks again (when the list or drawer is open)

note: THREE (0.141 build/three.min.js global) is loaded first. The wheel blocks page scroll over the panel and is used for walking, so use it on panels that cover the whole screen (pages without scroll). The original cart·box models are replaced by wire-rod instances and wheels, and the environment photo by a skin-colored studio strip. The floor is --kf-ink mixed 36% into --kf-bg, and the fog is --kf-surface mixed 55% into --kf-bg. The original product display’s “visitor count · restock vote” was dropped.
